signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Intervention Risk
signals.text: CAD/JPY momentum leads G10 performance with a 1.575% leader-to-laggard spread, the widest current bilateral theme. CAD (1W avg +0.799%) benefits from a positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +11.6, while JPY remains the G10 laggard (1W avg -0.776%) despite a high JPY ESI of +16.3. The 125bp BoC-BoJ OIS carry differential sustains the CAD bid, but verbal intervention warnings from former official Furusawa highlight that the MoF remains active in monitoring yen levels. USD/JPY trading at 159.45 sits just below the 160.00 threshold previously associated with direct action, creating a high-beta risk for CAD/JPY if a JPY short-squeeze is triggered. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY; carry and data outperformance favor CAD while intervention risk caps JPY weakness. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: BoJ verbal warnings escalate to confirmed intervention, forcing a rapid liquidation of JPY-short carry trades.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Put Skew + Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.45 is holding below its SMA20/50 cluster (160.65/161.12), following cooler-than-expected US inflation data. The 25d Risk Reversal (RR) shows a strong put skew of -2.07, indicating the options market is paying a significant premium for USD/JPY downside protection despite the 264bp OIS carry advantage for USD. This options divergence suggests institutional hedging against BoJ intervention or a September rate hike, which Furusawa notes is likely. The negative -1.4% Vol Risk Premium (VRP) reflects a dangerous complacency in realized volatility relative to the rising policy and intervention risks. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; options skew and intervention risk outweigh nominal carry advantage. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: US 10Y yields rebound sharply, reasserting the carry dominance and overrunning intervention threats.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5856 has recovered from recent lows, trading above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5847/0.5787/0.5834). RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The negative real rate of -1.56% in New Zealand remains accommodative, but the data outperformance suggests the spec short position is increasingly crowded and vulnerable to a squeeze. Fading Fed hike bets following softer US PPI and CPI data provide the macro tailwind for this NZD recovery. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; asymmetric squeeze potential against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: NZD/USD daily close below the SMA200 at 0.5834 invalidates the recovery thesis.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rate Support
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3491 remains technically constructive, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3424/1.337/1.3414). The pair exhibits a massive +5.1% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 5.9%), signaling that the options market is pricing in significantly more volatility than has been realized over the last 30 days. This elevated premium suggests heavy institutional hedging around the 1.3500 handle. Fundamentally, the GBP real rate of +0.93% is significantly more restrictive than the EUR's +0.09%, supporting GBP outperformance on a relative policy basis within Europe. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; technical position and real rate differential favor upside. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — market bias hold. Risk: A sharp compression in the VRP via a collapse in IV would suggest the trend is losing its protective hedge-bid.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + Commodity Neutrality
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7062 is trading above its key moving average cluster (SMA20/50/200: 0.7019/0.6993/0.6937). Retail sentiment is heavily skewed at 75% short, diverging from the institutional COT positioning where Leveraged Funds are net long +37,990 (72.1% long). This setup typically suggests a continuation of the uptrend as retail traders unsuccessfully attempt to fade the move. While WTI oil remains subdued below $80.50 due to Hormuz reopening efforts, the 73bp AUD carry advantage over USD SOFR continues to provide a structural floor for the pair. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional long positioning and retail-short fuel support trend. Catalyst: RBA Bullock speech today. Risk: AUD/USD close below SMA20 (0.7019) signals a shift in momentum.
